question: What does nutrient quality primarily refer to in dietetics?

options.A: The total financial cost of the food items consumed
options.B: The nutritional value, density, and health-promoting properties of foods
options.C: The total number of calories a food item contains regardless of source
options.D: The expiration date and physical shelf-life of processed food

explanation: Nutrient quality refers to the nutritional value, density, and health-promoting properties of the foods consumed, rather than just calorie count or cost. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h1)

question: Why is understanding nutrient quality particularly vital for nursing students in Nigeria?

options.A: To assist patients with luxury meal planning
options.B: Due to the prevalence of malnutrition, stunting, and diet-related chronic diseases
options.C: Because imported foods are the only option for adequate nutrition
options.D: To calculate exact hospital food service budgets

explanation: Understanding nutrient quality is crucial in Nigeria due to the high prevalence of malnutrition, stunting, and diet-related chronic diseases in various communities. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h1)

question: What defines a complete protein source?

options.A: It contains only plant-derived amino acids
options.B: It has high sugar and low fiber content
options.C: It contains all nine essential amino acids
options.D: It must be artificially fortified in a laboratory

explanation: Complete proteins contain all nine essential amino acids required by the human body for proper growth and cellular maintenance. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h2)

question: Which of the following describes the characteristics of high-quality carbohydrates?

options.A: High fiber content and low degree of processing
options.B: High glycemic index with rapid sugar absorption
options.C: Composed entirely of refined white flour and added sugars
options.D: Absence of any complex starches or dietary fiber

explanation: High-quality carbohydrates are unrefined, rich in dietary fiber, and provide sustained energy without causing rapid blood sugar spikes. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h2)

question: What does micronutrient bioavailability mean?

options.A: The total weight of vitamins measured in a raw food sample
options.B: The proportion of ingested vitamins and minerals successfully absorbed and used by the body
options.C: The monetary cost of vitamin and mineral supplements
options.D: The rate at which minerals expire on a grocery shelf

explanation: Bioavailability measures the actual fraction of an ingested nutrient that makes it into systemic circulation and is utilized by body tissues. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h3)

question: Which dietary combination enhances the absorption of non-heme iron?

options.A: Pairing non-heme iron with black tea containing tannins
options.B: Consuming non-heme iron alongside foods rich in vitamin C
options.C: Eating raw grains without soaking or fermenting them
options.D: Eliminating all dietary fats from the meal

explanation: Vitamin C acts as a reducing agent that converts non-heme iron into a more absorbable form in the gastrointestinal tract. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h3)

question: What happens when vegetables are boiled for a long time in excessive water and the water is discarded?

options.B: Water-soluble vitamins leach into the water and are lost
options.C: Minerals multiply rapidly due to heat activation

explanation: Boiling vegetables in excess water causes water-soluble vitamins like vitamin C and B vitamins to leach out, reducing the overall nutritional value if the water is thrown away. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h4)

question: Which traditional processing method helps reduce anti-nutrients and enhances mineral digestibility in grains?

options.A: Prolonged exposure to direct sunlight without cover
options.B: Deep frying in refined vegetable oil
options.D: Adding excessive table salt to raw grains

explanation: Traditional methods like fermentation and sprouting break down anti-nutrients such as phytates, thereby improving the bioavailability of minerals. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h4)

question: Which laboratory technique is commonly used to precisely measure vitamin concentrations in food samples?

options.B: Manual visual inspection under standard lighting

explanation: High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) is an advanced laboratory method used for precise separation and quantification of vitamins in food. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h5)

question: What is the clinical purpose of combining dietary assessments with blood tests like serum ferritin?

options.A: To calculate the exact economic cost of weekly groceries
options.B: To evaluate how well dietary nutrient quality translates into internal physiological health
options.C: To determine the patient's exact daily caloric expenditure during sleep
options.D: To test for food allergies and environmental sensitivities

explanation: Combining dietary surveys with biochemical markers like serum ferritin helps verify whether dietary intake is meeting the body's actual physiological needs. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h5)

question: What is a clinical consequence of consuming a diet low in protein and overall nutrient quality in pediatric patients?

options.A: Rapid muscle hypertrophy and enhanced athletic performance
options.B: Protein-energy malnutrition syndromes such as kwashiorkor or marasmus
options.C: Permanent immunity against all infectious diseases

explanation: Poor nutrient quality, particularly a lack of quality protein and energy, leads to severe deficiency syndromes like kwashiorkor and marasmus in children. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h6)

question: How does poor nutrient quality affect surgical or critically ill patients?

options.A: It accelerates wound healing and shortens hospital stays
options.B: It has no measurable impact on postoperative recovery
options.C: It impairs wound healing, delays recovery, and increases complication rates
options.D: It permanently lowers baseline blood pressure

explanation: Inadequate nutrient intake impairs collagen synthesis and causes muscle catabolism, resulting in delayed wound healing and increased complications. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h6)

question: What is a core recommendation of food-based dietary guidelines for optimizing nutrient intake?

options.A: Relying primarily on heavily processed, packaged foods for convenience
options.B: Encouraging dietary diversity, moderation, and whole foods
options.C: Eliminating all carbohydrates and fats entirely from the diet
options.D: Consuming only animal-based products to avoid anti-nutrients

explanation: Guidelines emphasize diversity, moderation, and the consumption of whole foods to ensure comprehensive nutrient intake. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h7)

question: According to the plate method mentioned in dietary guidelines, what proportion of the plate should ideally be filled with vegetables and fruits?
explanation: The standard plate method recommends filling one-half of the plate with colorful vegetables and fruits to ensure adequate micronutrient and fiber intake. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h7)
